details:
Android/Quest worlds are currently limited to 100 MB compressed, and the SDK blocks any upload above that. There’s no documented way to request more.

That said, some popular worlds appear to have Android builds well over 100 MB.(Example: FISH!) If there’s an exception process, it isn’t documented anywhere, which means most creators don’t know it exists or how to use it.

This matters a lot for creators who sell content or depend on world traffic. Staying under 100 MB often means lowering texture resolution, compressing audio further, or cutting content from the Quest version entirely, while some larger worlds can offer more on the same hardware.

Which is an unfair market advantage.

Suggestions:

Document any exceptions: if larger Android builds can be approved, explain the criteria and how to apply.

Open a review process: let any creator submit a world that needs more than 100 MB, judged on real Quest performance and memory use, not only download size.

Or consider raising the limit: if worlds above 100 MB run well on current Quest hardware, it may be time to raise the limit for everyone.

I think the limit itself is reasonable. I’d just like the same rules and the same opportunities to apply to every creator, not just creators that have the privilege to be in direct contact with vrchat.

Related posts:

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/review-system-for-quest-worlds-aiming-for-over-100mb-filesize

title: Transparent, fair path for Android/Quest worlds over 100 MB
